title: Compassion, Hidden Members, and the Distinguishing Marks
summary: The Lord's compassion expressed and the distinguishing marks set upon the human. T59 unfolds the three compassions — at the registers of life-bearing, of the Divine Human, and of the going-forth call — by which the Lord is bent in sorrow over the soul's confusion. T60 names the four weepings of the rational: three at descent under necessity, and a fourth at the consummation over those who chose darkness. T61 expounds how the Lord stays hidden within while his shining and his speech go forth as visible eyes and tongue. T62 describes how the Divine Human, clothed in the natural, stood against the proprium and what became of the strong loves it swallowed. T63 names the three foundations of glory the Lord sets in the natural mind. T64 defines love as the bond of the Lord and hatred as the proprium's first death. T65 expounds the three distinctions set upon Adam — divine image, fivefold structural mold, and the seal of every cosmic power — with seven consequences that follow.
organizing_principle: From compassion (T59-T60 — the Lord's grief over the soul's tribulation), through the hidden vs. visible structure (T61), the First Man's standing for the soul (T62-T63), to the cosmic origin of love and hatred (T64) and the three exaltations of the human (T65). The section is a meditation on how the Lord stands with the soul in its formation — what is hidden, what is shown, what is fixed within, and what comes forth as visible mark.
